name: In My Eyes
label: Revelation
lede: A guitarist kicked out of Ten Yard Fight started a Boston straight edge band with one rule against X's on anything, made two records for Revelation, and quit before it got old.

eras.title: Two months after Ten Yard Fight
eras.text: Boston was in the middle of a youth crew revival, with Ten Yard Fight, Bane and Floorpunch. Anthony Pappalardo had just been thrown out of Ten Yard Fight, and In My Eyes set itself a few rules so it wouldn't sound like a copy of anything.

q: We weren't thinking too hard, we were just doing it.
years.h: In My Eyes form in Boston, named for a Minor Threat song
years.p: Two months after Anthony Pappalardo is kicked out of Ten Yard Fight, he starts In My Eyes with singer Sweet Pete, guitarist Jeff Neumann, bassist Damian Genuardi and drummer Luke Garro. The name is a [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] song title.
years.xp: The band had inner rules: no wearing old band shirts, no X imagery even though they were all straight edge, no songs directly about straight edge, and real energy live. Pappalardo says they were playing tight within two months.

years.h: In My Eyes' demo sells several thousand copies
years.p: All-original songs, nothing carried over from Ten Yard Fight. Revelation says the demo sold several thousand copies before the band signed; Pappalardo still thinks it beats the album versions.

eras.title: Pushead on the cover
eras.text: Revelation signed the band, and The Difference Between came with artwork by the man who drew for Metallica and SSD. Then Revelation put them in a van with its West Coast and Boston bands for the summer.

years.p: Ten new songs plus reworked demo tracks, recorded at Salad Days in Boston with [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] of [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]]. Cover art by [[Pushead|404f318c-a6c4-43ed-892a-a431d0ad4b2b]]; first pressing 213 yellow and 104 red.
years.xp:
Pushead's name mattered to this crowd: he'd drawn for [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]], the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] and [[SSD|ee3fc3fc-1b89-423c-8310-bd06c10616ee]]. Pappalardo later called the album too dry and polished next to the demo.

In the press, the band said they weren't trying to emulate a genre, just play hardcore the way they'd want to hear it.

years.h: In My Eyes on Revelation's summer tour with Battery
years.p: In My Eyes tour with [[Speak 714|843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635]], [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]] and [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] on a Revelation Records summer package, on top of steady weekend runs out of Boston.

eras.title: Nothing to Hide, then enough
eras.text: Down to one guitar, In My Eyes made a heavier, catchier second album, covered a D.C. band from the Dischord catalog, took it to Europe, and ended the band on National Edge Day.

q: Some people complained about the album being more melodic, which is trippy to me.
years.p: One guitar now, with Jeff Neumann gone, and Brian McTernan producing again. Includes a cover of [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]]'s What's Wrong With Me? from the Void/Faith split.
years.xp:
Pappalardo wanted heavier riffs, catchier songs and better lyrics. Some fans complained it was too melodic; the breakdown in On My Side was not standard youth crew. He wished it had more reverb.

Revelation's first pressing was 500 white and 220 clear, and a second pressing of 330 blue was sold on the band's European tour.

years.h: In My Eyes' last show falls on the second National Edge Day
years.p: In My Eyes play their final show in October 2000, on the second National Edge Day. Pappalardo says anything more would have been overkill.
years.xp: Members also played in [[The Explosion|9cba6b36-ed3a-44d5-85d8-bc4181905f41]], [[Fastbreak|6ca65199-3330-4cb6-8589-f57930d60c28]] and Panic; Damian Genuardi played bass in The Explosion. Pappalardo became a writer, including the hardcore book Radio Silence.

years.h: Edge Day 2000: In My Eyes' last show
yt: Edge Day 2000: In My Eyes' last show

eras.title: Back in the Middle East
eras.text: Revelation kept both albums in print on new colors of vinyl, and In My Eyes came back once, for a sold-out Boston benefit.

years.h: Revelation repress both In My Eyes albums
years.p: Revelation presses 513 purple copies of The Difference Between and 556 green of Nothing to Hide, then another 550 clear and 330 grey in 2013.

years.h: In My Eyes reunite at the Middle East for a benefit
years.p: In My Eyes play a sold-out benefit for longtime Boston scene member Jarrod Shanahan at the Middle East in Cambridge, with [[The Rival Mob|06f73938-04f9-4b08-adc3-2978bb957de9]] and Boston Strangler. Resale tickets reportedly hit $60.
years.xp: Sweet Pete told the crowd he was fulfilling a childhood dream: playing a cover his first punk band, at thirteen, couldn't pull off. The Rival Mob and Boston Strangler traded the stage every few songs.

years.h: Sweet Pete, Pappalardo and Genuardi revisit Nothing to Hide
years.p: Sweet Pete, Anthony Pappalardo and Damian Genuardi spend two hours on Nothing to Hide for episode 80 of the Where It Went podcast, which works through the Revelation catalog record by record.
